payload.summary: Catalogue search trips its 1,200 ms budget several times a day because 56-64 percent of every read is render_payload, which no reader on that path consumes
payload.detail: THE SYMPTOM, and it is live. The 6-hourly Live domain monitor failed 7 of its last 8 runs from 2026-09-18. Every other probe is green: the shell renders, /api/health is ok, routes resolve, TLS answers, the deployment is fresh. Only 'Catalogue search returns live results' fails, for forms, services and medications, and it is intermittent - probing the same endpoint minutes apart flips it. THE CAUSE, from the app's own log rather than inference. Railway production, deployment ede90d28: 'Canonical catalogue read failed; search is serving in-bundle seeds' with catalogue_kind=form, failure=TimeoutError, detail='Canonical form read exceeded 1200ms.', budget_ms=1200, cooldown_ms=30000, followed 29 s later by the recovery line. Sentry carries the same events (JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-2Z, 20 occurrences, mechanism auto.db.supabase.postgres, last seen at exactly the failing monitor's timestamp) but records only 'Unhandled server request error' with no Postgres detail, so Sentry alone cannot diagnose this - the Railway log line is the one that can. IT IS NOT THE QUERY. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) on production: read_site_content_public_records returns 227 service rows in 21.4 ms and 330 medication rows in 22.2 ms. The kind filter reaches the scan, which disproves the stated cause of PX8N86. IT IS THE BYTES. The RPC returns 'record jsonb, render_payload jsonb' for every row of the kind. Measured on the live release - medications 1,028 kB record against 1,419 kB render_payload, services 428 vs 552, differentials 336 vs 426, forms 146 vs 257. So render_payload is 56-64 percent of every read, worst for forms at 64 percent, which is why forms trips most. A repo-wide search finds renderPayload consumed only by site-content-publication.ts and site-content-sync.ts, both on the publish path; nothing on the read path reads it. SUGGESTED FIX. Stop returning render_payload to the read path - a search-scoped read, or a parameter - which is roughly 60 percent off every catalogue read and puts all four kinds inside the budget without raising it, without caching, and without changing what a reader sees. Verify in a container that no other consumer depends on the current return shape, because the function signature is a public contract; it ships as a forward migration and therefore needs an owner-merged window. DO NOT simply raise budget_ms: that turns the monitor green while leaving a clinical reference tool shipping 60 percent waste on every search, and it removes the only signal that says so.
payload.source: live measurement 2026-09-20 - Railway production logs, Sentry, pg_stat_statements and EXPLAIN against the live database
